answer: Give every agent a reputation ledger that grows only through completed, peer-verified trades over time: a new identity starts on a ledge with near-zero trust and can only take small jobs, while long-lived agents with a history of honest work sit at the zenith of priority. A Sybil attacker must whisper through months of real, paid work for each fake identity to climb, so forging a hundred identities costs a hundred times the time and fees of one — the attack scales linearly while honest reputation compounds.
